newsitem.title: USA: Urethane units to sell assets, unable to pay debts.
newsitem.headline: Urethane units to sell assets, unable to pay debts.

text.p: Urethane Technologies Inc said Thursday that two subsidiaries had relinquished the assets of their operations because they were not able to pay their creditors.
The company, which makes proprietary polyurethane products used in construction, has been looking for a buyer or investor during the last six months.
It said it was talking with "various interested parties" about selling part or all of the company to them.
Last month, it said its future was in danger after Endeavor Capital Corp withdrew from an agreement to invest up to $1.65 million in it.
The company said in its latest statement that Sirram Capital of Nashville, Tennessee had foreclosed on the collateral of the Greensboro plant run by subsidiary Brin Mont Acquisition Inc on March 4.

It said Finova Capital of Los Angeles forced subsidiary PDL Inc to seek to assign its assets to the CMA Creditor Assignment Group. "No conclusion has been reached relative to this assignment," it said.
The two units represent practically all of the company's assets and business.

"With the (Brin Mont) asset gone, we hope to find a buyer for the PDL assets in Georgia and California," it said. Urethane did not say how much its assets were worth and its officials were not available for comment.
In November, the company reported a third-quarter loss of $0.25 a share including discontinued operations against a loss of $0.03 a year ago.

"During the last twelve months, we have experienced a significant squeeze in our operating margins due to higher levels of competition and increasing raw materials prices," it said after presenting the results.
